messages:
devops-deploy-bot: Scheduled deploy: v1.14.2 -> prod in 20m. Changelog auto-generated: 'Telemetry: change default to enabled for internal clients (opt-out available)'.

alice: Wait, is that a patch or a minor? This is just a default toggle, no API change. :thinking_face:

ben: It's a behavioral default change, but it doesn't change public API shape. Our semver doc says patch for behavior that is backward-compatible. I lean patch.

cara: Historically we've bumped minor when default changes affect data collection or legal surface. This touches telemetry defaults — ops + legal should sign off.

dave: Legal flagged retention wording last week, but I checked with them earlier: no contract-level change. They said proceed but note in release notes.

eve: Two practical things: 1) customers could notice additional metrics being sent (opt-out path still exists). 2) our release-note generator filters 'internal-only' tags; make sure this appears in public notes.

frank: There's also a transitive dep bump here — protobuf pinned to 4.0.1 to fix a parsing bug. That is semver-minor on protobuf, but for our repo it's a deps-only change. Do we count deps-only as patch?

alice: Our rule has been: deps-only -> patch, unless it unlocks new public API features. So patch for us.

ben: Another tagging question: do we tag the CI artifact with +ci metadata (e.g., v1.14.2+ci.212345) and then create a clean release tag v1.14.3? I prefer not to publish +buildmeta as the canonical release tag.

cara: Agreed. We should avoid +buildmeta for release tags because our deploy automation treats tags with + as non-canonical. Use CI tags for artifacts, and bump semver for the release.

release-ops: Proposal: create v1.14.3 as the patch release that includes the telemetry toggle + protobuf pin. Release notes will have a 'privacy/telemetry' callout and link to opt-out doc. Canary rollout 10% for 30m, then 100% if no errors. Rollback plan: auto-rollback to v1.14.2 on error ratio > 0.5% in 15m.

ben: Sounds good. Suggest the tag message include the changelist and legal ack: "patch: enable telemetry default for internal clients; protobuf pin; legal reviewed".

alice: For transparency, I'd like the git commands noted so release-ops can run them quickly: 
```
# create annotated tag
git tag -a v1.14.3 -m "patch: telemetry opt-out default; protobuf pin; legal ack"
git push origin v1.14.3
```

frank: Small nit: our release checklist requires updating release-notes.md in the release branch before tagging. I'll open a tiny PR for the note right now.

devops-deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for v1.14.3 -> prod at 2123456805 (10% traffic). Monitoring hooks: latency, error-rate, telemetry ingestion delta.

cara: :eyes: watching logs. If telemetry ingestion delta > expected by 2x, we pause canary.

dave: Also ensure the customer-facing announcement mentions the opt-out link explicitly. We had one upset last quarter when a feature flipped defaults silently.

eve: I'll add the opt-out link to the release note blurb. Also adding a short FAQ line.

release-ops: Tagging done, changelog updated, PR merged with release-notes.md. Pushing tag now.

devops-deploy-bot: Push succeeded, canary live. Will escalate on auto-rollback. :shipit: 

alice: tl;dr: patch bump to v1.14.3, avoid +buildmeta for canonical tag, deps-only counts as patch here, canary + rollback rules in place.

ben: One follow-up: update our semver guidelines doc to explicitly call out telemetry/default toggles as patch vs minor so this debate doesn't recur. I'll draft a short PR.

cara: Thanks everyone. Closing on this thread once canary passes or rollback occurs. :thumbsup:
